spec_match.rationale: Probes the proposal's one concrete new surface (entryType 'session-end' in supportedEntryTypes), demonstrates the exact failure class the explainer's use cases describe (abrupt termination losing final telemetry), and shows the shipped mitigation (fetchLater) the guidance recommends.

interactive.rationale: Three real experiments: a supportedEntryTypes probe that prints the browser's actual list, a worker graceful-vs-terminate() comparison whose final telemetry is a real POST verified by querying the reporting endpoint (not the worker's own messages), and a real fetchLater() deferred beacon.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb names the three experiments; the page delivers all three.

edge_cases.rationale: Missing PerformanceObserver, missing Worker, polyfilled (non-native) fetchLater, and missing fetchLater each get labelled fallbacks that never report fake success; worker verdicts are derived from observed outcomes with an explicit inconclusive state for late starts or zero-progress runs; the session-end probe can return true if a future browser ships it.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6594955352080384, the explainer's use-cases section, and MDN fetchLater.

conformance.rationale: The session-end-entry-type-proposed assertion in the feature suite mirrors this page's probe exactly, including the expected-fail framing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: probe printed 13 real entry types without session-end; the worker experiment is endpoint-grounded — graceful run delivered 5 progress messages and the reporting endpoint confirmed the final beacon arrived, terminate() run delivered 3 progress messages and the endpoint confirmed the beacon was never received; native fetchLater (name 'fetchLater', [native code]) returned {activated:false}; zero console errors and no failed requests; screenshots inspected.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the probe ran, both worker outcomes (graceful delivered / abrupt lost), and fetchLater scheduling or fallback.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; the delivered/lost verdicts use accent-emerald/accent-rose on the near-white paper background (AA for large bold text).

accessibility.rationale: Results table has a proper thead/scope structure and aria-label; every result panel is role=status; buttons are native and 44px tall.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: responsive-check matrix ok on both classes; the three stages stack cleanly at 360px with no overflow.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate delivered fetchLater beacon end-to-end
openQuestions.detail: Scheduling is verified ({activated:false}), but delivery could not be observed because the harness SIGKILLs the whole browser process, which is outside fetchLater's guarantee. A manual pass should navigate away normally and confirm the beacon lands at ../report.

guidanceConsulted.query: reliable end of session telemetry beacon delivery
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use fetchLater() for reliable end-of-session telemetry: schedule early, abort-and-reschedule on updates, let the browser own delivery; wrap calls in try/catch for quota errors.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Stage 3 implements exactly this pattern (AbortController re-scheduling, try/catch, browser-owned delivery) and the page copy explains why it is today's best answer.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve full-session-analytics run 2026-08-02; fetchLater() returned {activated:false} during CDP verification

guidanceConsulted.query: table pass fail state colour and text
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Convey pass/fail state with text, not colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The delivery table verdicts say 'yes — final message arrived' / 'NO — final message lost' in addition to the green/red colouring; the green was darkened via color-mix to pass AA at 0.9rem.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: computed contrast of color-mix(in srgb, --accent-emerald 75%, --text-black) on white ≈ 5.6:1 (>4.5:1)

summary: Verified with headless Chromium 141 over CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud routine): all three experiments exercised for real. The worker's final telemetry is a genuine network POST and both verdicts are read back from the reporting endpoint (graceful: beacon confirmed received; terminate(): beacon confirmed absent), with an explicit inconclusive state when the endpoint is unreachable or the worker never progressed. fetchLater is native here and scheduled cleanly. Console and network clean on desktop and mobile.
